definition_en: the indefinite article used before a singular noun that is not specific
core_image: 手里拿着一本书，只是随便一本
scene: 文具店里，学生挑了一支蓝色的笔。She bought a blue pen at the shop.
sceneCN: 这里 a 是「一（个）」（第 1 个义项：指单个事物）；句意为她在店里买了一支蓝色的笔。

senses.title: The indefinite article
senses.definition: used before a singular noun that is not specific
senses.definitionCN: 用在非特指的单数名词前
senses.example: I saw a dog in the park.
senses.exampleCN: 我在公园里看见一只狗。
senses.why: The form came from the old word for one, so it still points to a single, unspecified thing.
senses.whyCN: 它来自古英语表示「一」的词，所以仍指向一个不确定的单个事物。

senses.title: One of a class, in general
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean any one member of a class
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，泛指某一类中的任何一个
senses.example: A bird has wings.
senses.why: Because the article can pick any member of a class, it can also state a general truth about that class.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个冠词可以指同类中的任意一个，所以也能说明一整类事物的一般情况。

senses.title: A certain unknown person
senses.definition: used before a name when the speaker does not know the person
senses.definitionCN: 用在姓名前，表示说话人不清楚具体是谁
senses.example: A Mr. Lee is waiting at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一位姓李的先生在门口等候。
senses.why: Here the number sense fades into a name: the speaker knows only that one such person exists.
senses.whyCN: 这里数目感淡化，落在姓名上：说话人只知道有这么一个人，并不清楚是谁。

definition_zh: 能力；才能；本领；才智
definition_en: the power or skill needed to do something
core_image: 孩子第一次自己骑上自行车
scene: 操场上，一个孩子第一次自己骑上自行车。Her ability to ride alone surprised the class.
sceneCN: 这里 ability 是「能力」（第 1 个义项：做事的力量或本领）；句意为她独自骑车的能力让全班惊讶。

pos.zh: 名词：能力；才能；本领；才智

senses.title: Power to do something
senses.definition: the power or skill needed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做成某事所需的力量或本领
senses.example: She has the ability to solve hard problems.
senses.why: The noun is built on able, so it names the state of being able to do something.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 able 构成，直接表示「能够做成事」的状态。

senses.title: A special talent
senses.definition: a particular skill that stands out in one field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方面特别突出的本领
senses.example: He showed great ability in music.
senses.exampleCN: 他在音乐上表现出很强的才能。
senses.why: The general power narrows to one field, and that gives the sense of a special talent.
senses.whyCN: 把整体的能力缩小到某一方面，就成了特别突出的才能。

senses.title: A measured level of mind
senses.definition: the level of mental power a person has, seen in comparison
senses.definitionCN: 把不同人的才智放在一起比较所得的水平
senses.example: The test is for students of all abilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试面向各种才智水平的学生。
senses.why: When ability is compared across people, it becomes a level rather than a single power.
senses.whyCN: 当能力被放到不同人之间比较，它就从单一力量变成一种水平。

senses.title: On the subject of

senses.definitionCN: 以某事为谈论的话题

senses.why: About first meant around, and a topic is what a talk circles around, so it came to mean on the subject of.
senses.whyCN: about 原义是「在周围」，话题正是一段谈话围着转的东西，于是表示关于。

senses.title: Roughly a number
senses.definition: close to a number but not exact
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个数目但不精确
senses.example: About twenty pupils came.
senses.why: The sense of around moved from space to number, giving the meaning of roughly.
senses.whyCN: 「在周围」从空间转到数目，就得到大约的意思。

senses.title: In various places
senses.definition: in many places around a area
senses.definitionCN: 在一个区域内的多处地方
senses.example: They walked about the town.
senses.why: This keeps the oldest spatial picture: moving around within a place.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留最古老的空间画面：在一个地方内部四处走动。

senses.title: Just going to
senses.definition: used with to for something that will happen very soon
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，表示某事马上就要发生
senses.example: The train is about to leave.
senses.why: The picture of being around a point became being on the edge of an event, so about to marks what is just ahead.
senses.whyCN: 「在某一点周围」的画面变成「处在事件的边缘」，所以 about to 标记马上要做的事。

scene: 上课铃响后，教室后排有一个空座位。One pupil was absent from class today.
sceneCN: 这里 absent 是「缺席的」（第 1 个义项：不在场）；句意为今天有一名学生缺课。

pos.zh: 形容词：缺席的；不在的；缺乏的；心不在焉的

senses.title: Not present
senses.definition: not in the place where one should be
senses.definitionCN: 不在本应到场的地方
senses.example: Three pupils were absent today.
senses.why: Absent comes from Latin absens, being away, and it names the person who is not there.
senses.whyCN: absent 来自拉丁语 absens「不在场」，直接指人没有到场。

senses.title: Missing from a place
senses.definition: not found in a place where it is expected
senses.definitionCN: 在本该出现的地方找不到
senses.example: The old sign is absent from the wall.
senses.why: The sense of a person away was widened to things that are not where they belong.
senses.whyCN: 把「人不在」扩到事物，就表示某物在该处缺失。

senses.title: Not paying attention
senses.definition: with the mind somewhere else
senses.definitionCN: 心思在别处
senses.example: He wore an absent look in class.
senses.exampleCN: 他在课上显得心不在焉。
senses.why: The body is there but the mind is away, so absent also describes a wandering attention.
senses.whyCN: 人虽在场，心却「不在」，于是 absent 也形容注意力游移。

items.en: English used absent for people and for things that were missing.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 absent 指人不在，也指事物缺少。

items.en: Today it also describes a dreamy, unwatching mind.
items.cn: 今天它也形容走神、不留心的状态。

definition_zh: 接受；同意；承认；接纳
definition_en: to take something that is offered, or to agree to something
core_image: 伸手接过别人递来的礼物
scene: 生日会上，女孩伸手接过朋友递来的礼物。She accepted the gift with a smile.
sceneCN: 这里 accepted 是「接受」（第 1 个义项：收下别人给的东西）；句意为她笑着收下了礼物。

pos.zh: 动词：接受；同意；承认；接纳

senses.title: To take what is offered
senses.definition: to take something that someone offers
senses.definitionCN: 收下别人给予的东西
senses.example: She accepted the gift with a smile.
senses.why: Accept comes from Latin accipere, to take to oneself, so the first sense is simply taking what is offered.
senses.whyCN: accept 来自拉丁语 accipere「接过来」，本义就是把别人给的东西收下。

senses.title: To agree to a plan
senses.definition: to say yes to a plan or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法表示同意
senses.example: The class accepted the new rule.
senses.why: Taking something in the mind turns into agreeing with a proposal.
senses.whyCN: 把某物收进心里，就转为对提议表示同意。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to agree that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事是真的
senses.example: He accepted that he was wrong.
senses.why: A fact is taken in rather than pushed away, which gives the sense of admitting.
senses.whyCN: 把事实收进来而不是推开，就得到承认的意思。

senses.title: To take someone into a group
senses.definition: to let a person join a group
senses.definitionCN: 让某人加入一个群体
senses.example: The team accepted him as a member.
senses.why: Taking a person into a group is the social form of taking something offered.
senses.whyCN: 把一个人收进群体，是「收下给予之物」在人际关系上的形式。

definition_zh: 事故；意外；偶然；车祸
definition_en: something bad that happens by chance, or something that happens without a plan
core_image: 两辆车在路口相撞
scene: 雨天路滑，两辆车在路口相撞。The accident blocked the road for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 accident 是「事故」（第 1 个义项：意外发生的坏事）；句意为这起事故让道路堵了一个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：事故；意外；偶然；车祸

senses.title: A harmful unexpected event
senses.definition: an unexpected event that causes harm
senses.definitionCN: 造成伤害的意外事件
senses.example: The car accident blocked the road.
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to happen or to fall upon, and the word first named anything that happened without plan; harm became its usual meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「发生、降临」，这个词本指一切偶然发生的事，后来常指带来伤害的事故。

senses.title: Something done by chance
senses.definition: an event that happens without plan
senses.definitionCN: 没有计划却发生的事
senses.example: Meeting her was a happy accident.
senses.exampleCN: 遇见她是一次愉快的偶然。
senses.why: This keeps the old sense of chance, without the idea of harm.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留古老的「偶然」义，不带伤害的意味。

senses.title: Chance rather than plan
senses.definition: used in by accident for something not intended
senses.definitionCN: 用于 by accident，表示并非有意
senses.example: I found the letter by accident.
senses.why: By accident turns the noun into a phrase of manner, marking an action that was not planned.
senses.whyCN: by accident 把名词变成方式短语，标记并非计划中的行为。

senses.title: Happening by chance

senses.exampleCN: 那场火是意外，并非计划。

senses.whyCN: accident 加上形容词后缀 -al，构成描述「由偶然带来」的词。

senses.title: Not intended

senses.definitionCN: 做的时候并无本意

senses.why: The word moved from events to people's words and acts, where chance means not on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从事件转到人的言行，此时「偶然」就是并非故意。

items.en: The adjective ending -alis marked something that happens by chance.

items.en: Old French carried the adjective into English.

items.en: English used accidental for events that were not planned.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪用 accidental 指未计划的事件。

items.en: Today it also labels insurance damage and musical signs.

definition_en: to succeed in doing something after effort, or to reach a goal
core_image: 运动员冲过终点线
scene: 运动会上，选手全力冲过终点线。She achieved her best time in the final race.
sceneCN: 这里 achieved 是「取得」（第 1 个义项：经过努力做成某事）；句意为她在决赛中跑出了自己的最好成绩。

senses.title: To reach a goal
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching a goal
senses.definitionCN: 成功地到达目标
senses.example: We achieved our goal before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在中午前达到了目标。
senses.why: Achieve comes from Old French achever, to finish or to come to a head, so it first means reaching the end of a goal.
senses.whyCN: achieve 来自古法语 achever「完成、到达终点」，本义是把目标走到头。

senses.title: To gain a result by effort
senses.definition: to get a result through work
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力得到某种结果
senses.example: She achieved high marks in the test.
senses.exampleCN: 她在测验中取得了高分。
senses.why: Reaching an end was applied to results, so the word came to mean gaining marks or success.
senses.whyCN: 把「走到终点」用在结果上，就指靠努力取得分数或成功。

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.definition: to finish a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做完
senses.example: The team achieved the work on time.
senses.why: The oldest sense of finishing shows plainly when the object is a piece of work.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是一项工作时，最古老的「完成」义就清楚地显现出来。

senses.title: A great result
senses.definition: something important done through effort
senses.definitionCN: 靠努力做成的重要事情
senses.example: Winning the match was a great achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得比赛是一项了不起的成就。
senses.why: The ending -ment can name the result of the verb achieve, so the word first means a great result.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 可以指动词 achieve 的结果，所以这个词先表示了不起的成果。

senses.title: The act of reaching a goal
senses.definition: the act of reaching a goal

senses.example: The achievement of the goal took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 实现这个目标用了三年。
senses.why: The same ending can also name the act itself, which gives the sense of reaching a goal.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也可以指动作本身，于是有了「达到目标」这一层意思。

senses.title: A record of success
senses.definition: a record of success in study or work

senses.example: Her achievements in science won a prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的科学成绩赢得了一个奖项。
senses.why: When the results are listed together in study or work, achievement means a record of success.
senses.whyCN: 把成果放在学习或工作里排成记录，achievement 就指成绩与成就。

senses.definitionCN: 在电影或电视中表演的女子
senses.example: The actress won a film prize.
senses.exampleCN: 那位女演员赢得了一个电影奖项。
senses.why: Actress is the older female form of actor, used for a woman who performs in films or on television.
senses.whyCN: actress 是 actor 较早的女性形式，指在电影或电视中表演的女子。

senses.title: A woman on stage
senses.definition: a woman who performs in a theatre
senses.definitionCN: 在剧场里表演的女子
senses.example: The actress bowed to the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那位女演员向观众鞠躬。
senses.why: The same word serves for the stage, where the performance is given live in a theatre.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用于舞台，因为那是在剧场里现场表演。

intro.en: The recorded history of actress is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 actress 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Actor meant a doer, the base of the English word.
items.cn: actor 意为做事的人，是英语词的基干。

items.en: French added a feminine ending to make a woman doer.
items.cn: 法语加上女性词尾，指女性做事者。

items.en: English actress became common for women on the stage.
items.cn: 英语中 actress 逐渐成为舞台上女性的常用词。

items.en: The word spread with the growth of theatres and films.
items.cn: 随着剧院与电影的发展，这个词传播开来。

items.en: Today many writers prefer actor for both women and men.
items.cn: 今天许多作者对男女都用 actor。

definition_zh: 实际上；事实上；竟然；真正地
definition_en: in fact, or really, or used to correct what was said
core_image: 有人说错了，另一个人摆手纠正
scene: 同学说今天不上课，老师摇头纠正他。Actually, the class begins at nine.
sceneCN: 这里 actually 是「实际上」（第 1 个义项：说明真实情况）；句意为实际上这节课九点开始。

pos.zh: 副词：实际上；事实上；竟然

senses.title: In fact
senses.definition: used to state what is really true
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明真正的情况
senses.example: Actually, the answer is easy.
senses.why: Actual plus -ly makes an adverb that points to the fact rather than the appearance.
senses.whyCN: actual 加 -ly 构成副词，指向事实而不是表面看起来的样子。

senses.title: Really, to one's surprise
senses.definition: used to stress something surprising that did happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调出乎意料却真的发生的事
senses.example: She actually finished the whole book.
senses.why: From stating a fact, the word took on the task of stressing a surprising truth.
senses.whyCN: 从陈述事实进一步用于强调令人意外的真相，就有了「竟然」的口气。
